title: Introduce partition-aware eviction thermostat and soft-restore probe protocol
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds a partition-aware eviction controller and a soft-restore probe to reduce oscillatory evictions during transient regional overloads; ships as a staged rollout behind feature flag.
description: Motivation: We observed repeated tenant eviction oscillations when a subset of nodes in a region experienced transient KV cache pressure or short-lived network flakiness. These oscillations impact tail latency and cause cascading failovers even when upstream capacity is recoverable quickly. This change implements a partition-aware eviction thermostat (Thermostat) that smooths eviction decisions across AZs and a Soft-Restore Probe that verifies node stability before bulk reinstates. Design: 1) Thermostat - tracks per-partition eviction pressure as an exponentially-weighted metric combining queued requests, KV memory pressure, and observed local rejection rates. It computes a soft target eviction rate per-partition and then applies a staggered drain schedule with jitter to avoid synchronized restarts. The thermostat supports per-tenant weighting and respects tenant SLO budgets so high-priority tenants are least affected. 2) Soft-Restore Probe - before restoring a quarantined/evicted route or rebalancing workloads back into a node, the probe performs lightweight health checks including a KV warm-read, a small synthetic inference with the fast-path model, and a short-lived KV pressure soak to detect reentrance risk. Probe results are weighted into the thermostat's hysteresis window to prevent immediate flip-flops. 3) Cross-AZ coordination - Thermostat uses the existing gossip channel to publish compact pressure tokens (no PII) so neighboring AZs can coordinate a gentle redistribution rather than abrupt evictions. 4) Feature gating & rollout - guarded by runtime feature flag partition_eviction_thermostat_v1; default off for all accounts, on-by-default in a canary org, and phased cluster rollout using Console rollout tasks. Implementation notes: - Core logic in runtime/eviction/thermostat.go with clear interfaces for metrics and probes. - Probe implementation in runtime/eviction/soft_restore_probe.go with pluggable checks. - Config in runtime/config/eviction.yaml with defaults tuned after offline trace replay. - Telemetry: new metrics eviction_thermostat_target_rate, eviction_thermostat_actual_rate, soft_restore_probe_latency_ms, soft_restore_probe_pass_ratio. - Small integration harness in test/integration/eviction_thermostat_test.go that replays a recorded spike and verifies no >2x eviction oscillation within 5m. Risks & mitigations: - Risk: additional coordination traffic could increase control plane load. Mitigation: pressure tokens are compact and rate-limited; added a backpressure-limit in gossip publisher. - Risk: probe false negatives preventing needed restores. Mitigation: probe uses multiple signals and falls back to manual override; feature gated to allow quick disable. Testing & validation: Unit tests for heuristic boundaries and probe outcomes; integration replay against recorded incidents/region-panics; synthetic canary with gradual traffic ramp. Rollout plan: enable in canary region for 48h with aggressive telemetry dashboards; if pass, enable in 20% of clusters for 24h, then global 100% in 3 stages. Observability: dashboards added under Console -> Serving -> Eviction Thermostat; alerts added: thermostat_target_actual_divergence > 2x for 10m, probe_pass_ratio < 90% for 5m. Related: closes ENG-1829 and mitigates recurring alerts in SRE-INC-1102. Why this differs from existing approaches: Instead of hard, fast evictions or purely local heuristics, this design pairs soft-targeted eviction rates with a probe-driven rejoin handshake and cross-AZ coordination so restores are deliberate and less likely to trigger ripples.
